  "situation": "At the Command Post on the night of 16 April 1961, a presidential order had canceled the planned D-Day air attacks following a recommendation from the Department of State. Higher authority had directed that D-Day air attacks be more limited. The Commander warned senior officials that the opposing air force retained dangerous fighter and bomber capability and that the landing force's supply ships could be sunk. An assessment after earlier strikes estimated that about half of the opposing tactical aircraft had been knocked out. The ships were close to the transport area, and the Commander reported that a withdrawal message would arrive after landing operations were underway. After conferring with senior intelligence officials, the Secretary of State recommended keeping the cancellation in place.",
